root_cause.text: The inline assembly output constraint for the `vstl` instruction indicates only a one-byte write, while the instruction actually writes a runtime-variable number of bytes (at least two when `index > 0`), causing KMSAN to false-positively treat the unwritten portion of the memory as uninitialized.
root_cause.evidence: The commit description states: "An inline assembly instruction 'vstl' can write varied amount of bytes depending on value of 'index' argument ... clang generates kmsan write helper call depending on inline assembly constraints. Constraints are evaluated compile-time, but value of 'index' argument is known only at runtime. clang currently generates call to __msan_instrument_asm_store with 1 byte as size." The patch adds `kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size)` after the inline asm to inform KMSAN of the actual number of bytes written.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add include for linux/kmsan.h to enable KMSAN instrumentation in the header.
intent_record.what: Added '#include <linux/kmsan.h>' to the existing header includes within the #ifndef __ASSEMBLER__ block, between the includes for linux/instrumented.h and asm/asm-extable.h.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the KMSAN (Kernel Memory Sanitizer) header is included when the header is compiled in non-assembler context, making KMSAN macros and functions available for use in the header file and its consumers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add KMSAN unpoison call after inline assembly store to suppress false-positive uninitialized memory detection.
intent_record.what: Added call to kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size) after inline assembly store in fpu_vstl function.
intent_record.how: Prevents KMSAN from reporting false-positive uninitialized memory warnings by explicitly marking the memory written by inline assembly as initialized.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add KMSAN unpoison call after inline assembly to suppress false positive uninitialized memory reports.
intent_record.what: Added a call to kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size) after the inline assembly block in function fpu_vstl.
intent_record.how: The change explicitly marks the memory region written by the inline assembly as initialized to the Kernel Memory Sanitizer (KMSAN), preventing false positive warnings about uninitialized memory.
